title: Electric Blue Waves: Chennai's Beaches Are Glowing — Here's How to Catch It
excerpt: Surfers and fishermen report the sea lighting up electric blue off Kovalam and Thiruvanmiyur this month. The plankton behind it is unpredictable — but here's when and where to look.
body:
• Waves off Chennai's Kovalam beach have repeatedly lit up electric blue this month, with sightings also reported at Thiruvanmiyur — caused by the plankton Noctiluca scintillans.
  • The glow appears in the deep night: surfers have spotted it around 3:30 a.m. at Kovalam and 4:50 a.m. at Thiruvanmiyur. It is unpredictable — some nights it simply doesn't appear.
  • Heavy rain and warm sea-surface temperatures create the nutrient conditions that trigger the blooms, according to a National Centre for Coastal Research case study of the 2019 occurrence.
  • Planning a trip? Head to Kovalam or Thiruvanmiyur between 2 a.m. and 5 a.m. on the darkest nights of the month, during and just after the monsoon — and ask local surf schools and fishermen, who track it daily.

At around 3:30 a.m. last Tuesday, surfer Saravanan B — who runs Saro Surf School at Kovalam — was making his way into the sea when the waves lit up in electric blue. Since word of the sighting made the rounds, inquisitive onlookers have been gathering along the shore from dusk till dawn to catch a fleeting glimpse of the phenomenon first hand.

"I spotted it in 2024 too, and it was such a spectacular sight," Saravanan told The Hindu. "I have witnessed it multiple times this month. But we can't plan an outing around it because it is unpredictable. Last night, we went to see it, but it did not make an appearance."

He is not the only one. Chennai resident Sujith Sivakumar recounted a sighting at Thiruvanmiyur beach at around 4:50 a.m. on Thursday: "Seeing the waves glow with an ethereal blue light against the dark shoreline felt completely surreal like something straight out of a fantasy film." A fishing community leader said many fishermen have spotted the glow in the waters off Kovalam this season as well.

"Seeing the waves glow with an ethereal blue light against the dark shoreline felt completely surreal like something straight out of a fantasy film."

— Sujith Sivakumar, on the Thiruvanmiyur sighting

What makes the sea glow

Bioluminescence is common in deep-sea organisms — jellyfish, squids, deep-sea shrimps and dinoflagellates — which use it to communicate and survive, notes ecologist Ranjit Daniels of Care Earth Trust. What lights up Chennai's shore is Noctiluca scintillans, a plankton that flashes blue when disturbed by waves.

The blooms are not random. A case study by Mishra et al. of the National Centre for Coastal Research found that after a spell of heavy rain in 2019, heterotrophic bioluminescent dinoflagellates appeared unusually along the Chennai coast. High atmospheric temperatures change the sea-surface temperature and increase dissolved nutrients; those conditions promote the growth of Thalassiosira, a microscopic algae, which in turn creates favourable conditions for Noctiluca scintillans to multiply rapidly. In short: monsoon runoff plus warm seas equals glowing surf.

Diaspora angle

For NRIs planning a Chennai visit this winter, this is the season's most magical — and most elusive — experience. The northeast monsoon months (October to December) are historically when the conditions align, and the glow typically shows in the pre-dawn hours on dark, moonless nights. Kovalam, about 40 km south of the city, and the more accessible Thiruvanmiyur beach are the two confirmed spots this season. Since the bloom can't be scheduled, treat it as a bonus on a late-night beach trip rather than the trip itself — and check with Saro Surf School or local fishermen, who watch the water daily.

What's next

As the monsoon deepens, more sightings are likely through November and December — but so is the unpredictability. The phenomenon is a reminder that the Bay of Bengal off Chennai is a living, shifting ecosystem. Catch it once, and you join a small club of people who have watched the sea turn the lights on.
